newsitem.title: FINLAND: Washington says Israel talks proposal useful.
newsitem.headline: Washington says Israel talks proposal useful.

text.p: The United States said on Thursday an Israeli proposal to speed up negotiations with the Palestinian Authority was "useful" but urged its chief Middle East ally to put the idea directly to the Palestinians.

Palestinians have dismissed the proposal on "final status" talks, put forward by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, as a publicity stunt to avoid the world's condemnation for breaking ground this week on a Jewish settlement.
White House press secretary Mike McCurry told reporters: "If either side has a proposal to make then they should do so directly to their negotiating counterpart. That's the purpose of negotiations."
"That's why exchanges face-to-face on matters like the timing and sequence of issues related to final status could be useful and would be more useful if they were done in direct dialogue," he said.
McCurry, who is with President Bill Clinton in Helsinki for a two-day summit with Russian President Boris Yeltsin, said Netanyahu's offer to finish making peace in six months could have value.

"We have always said that moving to the final status negotiations and beginning to deal with what are the most troublesome aspects of negotiations that the two sides have would be useful because that is where the greatest difficulty lies in resolving the differences that exist," he said.
Violence flared in the West Bank on Thursday over Israeli settlement building in Arab East Jerusalem and Jewish settlers opened a new front by moving into an Arab neighbourhood of the city.
